main_text.p: audebat. Gregorius iste finitis, anno Domini 998. mundum dereliquit, 3. sui pontificatus anno.
main_text.head: 8o. IOANNES decimusoctauus.
main_text.p: Ioannes decimusoctauus natione Græcus (de quo in prædicto Gregorio dictum est) hanc diabolicā Romanæ tyrannidis sedem, muneribus, tumultu, ac seditione, aliorum pontificum more ambiuit. Hic antea Placentinus episcopus erat, senex quidem doctus & diues, sed insatiabili mentis ardore papatum exoptans: quod illi exitium, diuina ultio- ne, perhorridum postea peperit. Tantum enim pecuniarum ex Constantinopoli secum Romam detulit, ut non solum prodentes, sed & constantes, suis largitionibus, ad maleficia impellere posset. Unde Crescentij Romani consulis potentia fretus, quem immensa pecunia corrupisse scribitur, Gregorio iniuriarum multarum, quod Germanus esset, incommodis profligato, per factionem pecuniæ conductam, papatum occupabat. De illis vero, quæ in illo ipso papatu cum suis sequacibus, mercatui expofuerit, Baptista Mantuanus in tertio Calamitatum libro, sic loquitur:
main_text.l: Ignes, thura, preces, cœlum est venale, Deus q;
main_text.p: Miror ego (inquit Platina) historicos, Ioan- nem

page.notes: Lower right corner text "nem" is a catchword-like fragment, and the final line is partly cut at the margin; "Ioan- nem" is the line-end split of "Ioannem". The top-left figure reads "158" (with the stroke of the 5 partly faded), and the mark "q;" at the end of the Deus line is a printed abbreviation for -que, left as printed. The text is heavily blurred in places (notably "ex Constantinopoli", "tumultu", "fretus"), so some letters are my best reading. Parts of the right and lower right margins are damaged by staining; no legible marginal notes are present. Scan shows show-through from the reverse side, which was not transcribed.
